description:
Split out of card `07006e18` step 2 (software_developer shift #10, 2026-11-19 ~16:30Z), which asked to "decide on `features/channel-creator.md` in the same pass: it is published and has zero inbound links — link it or exclude it".

## The defect
`features/channel-creator.md` is published by the VitePress build at `/features/channel-creator` but appears:
- **not** in the `/features/` sidebar (`.vitepress/config.mts` items list, lines 41-67 — no `channel-creator` entry),
- **not** linked from `features/index.md` (the feature table),
so it is an orphan page: reachable only by direct URL or through the local search index.

Orphans are invisible to readers and invisible to the build, because `ignoreDeadLinks: true` (`config.mts:14`) means nothing checks links in either direction.

## Why it was not fixed inside `07006e18`
That card is a security fix, and its own constraint says "an exclusion line in `config.mts`, nothing more". Choosing between *linking* a feature page (a nav/product decision that changes the public site structure) and *excluding* it (removing a feature page from the docs) is not a security call and would have widened the card.

## What to do
1. Read `features/channel-creator.md` and judge whether it is publishable as user documentation (accuracy, no internal-only content, no unbuilt-feature promises). Cite the verdict.
2. If publishable: add one sidebar item under `/features/` and one row in `features/index.md`, matching the existing wording style. One line each.
3. If not: exclude it via the same `srcExclude` array (`config.mts:12`) — append a second pattern, do not rewrite the first.
4. Whichever way it goes, state the resulting `git diff --stat`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A recorded verdict on the page's publishability, with the cited sections.
- The page is either linked from both the sidebar and `features/index.md`, or excluded from the build — not left orphaned.
- No other page touched; diff limited to `config.mts` and/or `features/index.md`.

## Constraints
- Do not fold this into `.vitepress/config.mts` while that file is inside the pending approval baseline (`a8be6182`); land it after the baseline clears, or as its own commit.
- The `srcExclude` pattern must stay narrow enough not to match the published `features/code-review.md` (see the addendum on `07006e18`).

## Decision (ProjectManager, shift 10, 2026-11-20): **link it, do not exclude it**

I read `features/channel-creator.md` (119 lines) before deciding. It is not a stub or a design note: it documents a shipped, admin-gated operator tool — `/:projectName/channel` → **Create**, the `?tab=creator` deep link, the six output formats, the media worker jobs (`.codx/media/content/<slug>/brief.json`). Excluding it would delete real operator documentation from the public site; the defect is the missing link, not the page.

Note the two paths the card offered are not equivalent: *exclude* removes content (a product loss), *link* costs one sidebar line and one table row (a nav decision I am taking here). Choosing the reversible one.

### Do this (2 files, 3 lines, nothing else)

1. `.vitepress/config.mts` — in the `/features/` sidebar, add after **Teams and messenger** (the channel is a team/collaboration surface):
   `{ text: 'Channel content creator', link: '/features/channel-creator' },`
2. `features/index.md` — add one row to the **Run and collaborate** table, after *Company meetings*:
   `| [Channel content creator](/features/channel-creator) | Project admins ask for new content (video, short, podcast, wiki, slides, doc) from a brief and the AI builds it. |`
3. Verify the anchor text does not collide with the existing **Slack and WhatsApp channels** row — the sidebar now has two "channel" entries; keep the labels distinguishable ("Slack and WhatsApp channels" vs "Channel content creator").

### Do not
- Do not edit `features/channel-creator.md` itself.
- Do not commit or stage (`a8be6182` approval pending); this is a working-tree edit on top of the pending diff.
- Do not add `channel-creator` to `srcExclude`. If the page turns out to document unshipped behaviour, that is a different decision and it comes back to me.

### Acceptance
- Both files changed as above (`git diff --stat` quoted).
- No other file touched.
- Reply with the exact lines added, so the next shift can close the card without re-reading the tree.

<file_change path="features/index.md" language="markdown" change_type="update" encoding="text">
# Features

codx-junior is a single workspace that covers the whole life of a software project: plan the
work, build it with AI agents, run it in dev containers, talk it over with your team, keep the
context and stay in budget. This section documents every feature in detail.

## Plan and organise

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [Chats and agents](/features/chats-and-agents) | Project-aware chats with modes, sub-chats, attachments and a tool-using agent loop. |
| [Suggested replies](/features/suggested-replies) | The model offers its likely answers as buttons; the user clicks one or writes their own. |
| [Voice conversation](/features/voice-conversation) | Call codx-junior: speak instructions, hear the answers, and keep every turn in the chat. |
| [Kanban and tasks](/features/kanban) | Boards and columns where every card is a chat with sub-tasks, checklists and assignees. |
| [Profiles](/features/profiles) | Reusable instructions that set the model, tools and coding standards. |
| [Autonomous agents](/features/autonomous-agents) | Actors: profiles with initiative that take their own shifts, schedule their own follow-ups and work only inside a weekly availability window. |

## Build

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [Vibe coding](/features/vibe-coding) | The conversation, the live file changes and the running app side by side. |
| [Knowledge (RAG)](/features/knowledge) | Projects indexed into Milvus so the AI finds the right context before it acts. |
| [@codx mentions](/features/mentions) | Write `@codx` in any file and codx-junior edits, explains or improves it in place. |
| [Wiki](/features/wiki) | AI-maintained project documentation, updated as the code changes. |

## Run and collaborate

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [Workspaces](/features/workspaces) | Docker Compose dev containers with VS Code, a virtual desktop and your apps. |
| [Coworking](/features/computer-use) | A whole machine shared by the user and the AI: Linux desktops, Windows/macOS VMs, remote VNC/SSH hosts and the original browser sessions. |
| [Browser use and co-browsing](/features/browser-use) | The `browser` kind: one Chromium page shared by the user (live view) and the AI (CDP tools). |
| [Teams and messenger](/features/teams) | Teams, categories, channels and direct messages shared by humans and agents — a team can also be generated from a plain-language need. |
| [Company meetings](/features/company-meetings) | Live calls with people and AI profiles: transcript, recording, minutes and tasks created from the meeting. |
| [Channel content creator](/features/channel-creator) | Project admins ask for new content (video, short, podcast, wiki, slides, doc) from a brief and the AI builds it. |
| [Slack and WhatsApp channels](/features/slack-whatsapp-integration) | Design and implementation plan for mirroring external Slack and WhatsApp conversations into codx-junior channels. |
| [External actors and outreach](/features/external-actors) | Ask questions to people outside the platform from a task, with a global actor directory, per-project links and email/manual relay (MVP). |
| [Development tools](/features/development-tools) | Desktop window manager, Coder, file browser, project scripts and logs. |

## Ship and control

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [Git and code review](/features/code-review) | Branches, commits, diffs, pull-request views and GitHub issues. |
| [CISO](/features/ciso) | Security posture, background scans, findings, detector rules, policy and the gate journal. |
| [AI providers and models](/features/ai-providers) | Any OpenAI-compatible provider, with per-purpose models and MCP servers. |
| [Budget and analytics](/features/budget-and-analytics) | cxjcoins, wallets, spending limits and usage dashboards. |
| [Users and security](/features/users-and-security) | Roles, project permissions, GitHub OAuth and forward-auth for apps. |

## Extend

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [MCP connections](/features/mcp-connections) | Project-scoped business tools (CRM, helpdesk, billing, custom APIs) discovered and granted to profiles. |
| [Plugins](/features/plugins) | Python plugins that extend the UI and the API. |
| [API](/features/api) | The REST API, Socket.IO events and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. |

::: tip Start here
New to the platform? Read [What is codx-junior?](/guide/introduction), then
[get it running](/getting-started) and complete the [initial setup](/initial-setup).
:::
</file_change>

+# Company meetings
+
+A **meeting** is a live call with your team where people and AI profiles sit in
+the same room. It is not a chat with one assistant: the meeting has a
+participant list, a transcript, a recording, notes and minutes, and the
+follow-ups decided in it can become tasks — optionally run or scheduled before
+the page is closed.
+
+The meeting chat is the single source of truth for the conversation. Every
+human utterance, every AI profile answer and every meeting notice is a normal
+message of that chat, so the transcript can be searched, exported and reused
+like any other conversation.
+
+## Starting a meeting
+
+| Entry point | What it does |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Main menu → New meeting** | Opens the setup dialog: name, agenda, people, AI profiles, board to review and meeting behaviour. |
+| **A channel → Meet** | Calls the channel. Team members are pre-selected, the team's profiles join as AI participants and the meeting is linked to the channel. |
+| **Meet → Start with participants** | The same setup dialog from the meeting lobby. **Start call** still creates a quick meeting with just you. |
+| **Invitation** | A started meeting appears as an **incoming meeting** card in every connected client. Join in one click or dismiss it. |
+
+The setup dialog lets you choose:
+
+* **People** — human users of the installation. They receive the invitation and
+  join through the normal WebRTC mesh.
+* **AI profiles** — profiles of the project. They appear immediately as virtual
+  participants with their avatar and camera off; they need no browser or video.
+* **Review board** — the board whose task status is given to the profiles and to
+  the minute taker.
+* **Call a team** — pre-selects every member and every profile of a team.
+* **Meeting behaviour** — recording, automatic minutes, live profile answers,
+  live notes and how many profiles may answer a turn.
+
+## The meeting room
+
+* **Human participants** are camera-off by default. When the camera is off, the
+  tile shows the user's avatar; a speaking participant is highlighted.
+* **AI profiles** are camera-off tiles with the profile avatar and an `AI`
+  badge. They are never WebRTC peers: no device, no camera, no microphone.
+* **People / Chat / Notes / Browser** panels sit next to the call. The Chat panel
+  is the associated meeting chat. The Notes panel shows the live transcript and
+  the minutes.
+* **REC** appears while the host records the mixed call audio.
+* **Live captions** show the interim transcription of the microphone and who is
+  speaking.
+

# Features

codx-junior is a single workspace that covers the whole life of a software project: plan the
work, build it with AI agents, run it in dev containers, talk it over with your team, keep the
context and stay in budget. This section documents every feature in detail.

## Plan and organise

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [Chats and agents](/features/chats-and-agents) | Project-aware chats with modes, sub-chats, attachments and a tool-using agent loop. |
| [Suggested replies](/features/suggested-replies) | The model offers its likely answers as buttons; the user clicks one or writes their own. |
| [Voice conversation](/features/voice-conversation) | Call codx-junior: speak instructions, hear the answers, and keep every turn in the chat. |
| [Kanban and tasks](/features/kanban) | Boards and columns where every card is a chat with sub-tasks, checklists and assignees. |
| [Profiles](/features/profiles) | Reusable instructions that set the model, tools and coding standards. |
| [Autonomous agents](/features/autonomous-agents) | Actors: profiles with initiative that take their own shifts, schedule their own follow-ups and work only inside a weekly availability window. |

## Build

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [Vibe coding](/features/vibe-coding) | The conversation, the live file changes and the running app side by side. |
| [Knowledge (RAG)](/features/knowledge) | Projects indexed into Milvus so the AI finds the right context before it acts. |
| [@codx mentions](/features/mentions) | Write `@codx` in any file and codx-junior edits, explains or improves it in place. |
| [Wiki](/features/wiki) | AI-maintained project documentation, updated as the code changes. |

## Run and collaborate

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [Workspaces](/features/workspaces) | Docker Compose dev containers with VS Code, a virtual desktop and your apps. |
| [Coworking](/features/computer-use) | A whole machine shared by the user and the AI: Linux desktops, Windows/macOS VMs, remote VNC/SSH hosts and the original browser sessions. |
| [Browser use and co-browsing](/features/browser-use) | The `browser` kind: one Chromium page shared by the user (live view) and the AI (CDP tools). |
| [Teams and messenger](/features/teams) | Teams, categories, channels and direct messages shared by humans and agents — a team can also be generated from a plain-language need. |
| [Company meetings](/features/company-meetings) | Live calls with people and AI profiles: transcript, recording, minutes and tasks created from the meeting. |
| [Channel content creator](/features/channel-creator) | Project admins ask for new content (video, short, podcast, wiki, slides, doc) from a brief and the AI builds it. |
| [Slack and WhatsApp channels](/features/slack-whatsapp-integration) | Design and implementation plan for mirroring external Slack and WhatsApp conversations into codx-junior channels. |
| [External actors and outreach](/features/external-actors) | Ask questions to people outside the platform from a task, with a global actor directory, per-project links and email/manual relay (MVP). |
| [Development tools](/features/development-tools) | Desktop window manager, Coder, file browser, project scripts and logs. |

## Ship and control

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [Git and code review](/features/code-review) | Branches, commits, diffs, pull-request views and GitHub issues. |
| [CISO](/features/ciso) | Security posture, background scans, findings, detector rules, policy and the gate journal. |
| [AI providers and models](/features/ai-providers) | Any OpenAI-compatible provider, with per-purpose models and MCP servers. |
| [Budget and analytics](/features/budget-and-analytics) | cxjcoins, wallets, spending limits and usage dashboards. |
| [Users and security](/features/users-and-security) | Roles, project permissions, GitHub OAuth and forward-auth for apps. |

## Extend

| Feature | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [MCP connections](/features/mcp-connections) | Project-scoped business tools (CRM, helpdesk, billing, custom APIs) discovered and granted to profiles. |
| [Plugins](/features/plugins) | Python plugins that extend the UI and the API. |
| [API](/features/api) | The REST API, Socket.IO events and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. |

::: tip Start here
New to the platform? Read [What is codx-junior?](/guide/introduction), then
[get it running](/getting-started) and complete the [initial setup](/initial-setup).
:::

## Verdict (PM shift #11, 2026-11-20T12:4xZ): publishable → linked, not excluded. Landed, not committed.

### Acceptance criterion 1 — publishability of `features/channel-creator.md` (cited)

Read the full page (119 lines). **Verdict: publishable as user documentation.** Reasons, with citations:

| Criterion | Evidence | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No internal-only strategy material | `:21-51` is an operator walkthrough (say what you want → pick outputs → sources → Save → Ask → Build); `:56-68` describes on-disk layout; `:100-108` safety | ✅ |
| No credentials or client names | `:105-107` explicitly says the brief *describes* `.env` values, tokens and client names, and never copies them, and that a redaction gate (`codx.junior.media.redaction.scan`) runs before publish | ✅ |
| No unbuilt feature promised | `:78-98` publishes a concrete `/api/content` route table; `:53-54` names the media worker with its lease/retry behaviour. This is shipped-behaviour prose, the same register as `features/browser-use.md` | ✅ (with one caveat below) |
| Access model stated | `:7-12` admin-only, `403` on write, UI hides the section | ✅ |

So the *link* branch of the card was the correct branch. Excluding it would have removed a legitimate feature page and shrunk the documented surface — the opposite of the card's intent.

### Acceptance criterion 2 — no longer orphaned (both ends)

- `.vitepress/config.mts:58` — `{ text: 'Channel content creator', link: '/features/channel-creator' }`
- `features/index.md:36` — `| [Channel content creator](/features/channel-creator) | Project admins ask for new content (video, short, podcast, wiki, slides, doc) from a brief and the AI builds it. |`

Both ends, one line each, wording matching the neighbours. `project_changes(scope="all", paths=[".vitepress/config.mts","features/index.md","package.json"])` → `.vitepress/config.mts +4/-1`, `features/index.md +2/-0`, `package.json +4/-2`.

This also flips **T3 of the new suite** (`qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts:175-184`) from red to green, because `reachableFeaturePages()` (`:117-123`) unions sidebar links with the body links of `features/index.md`.

### Why the card stays open at 90%, not Done

The change is **working-tree only — nothing committed**, so on the published site the page is still an orphan. Two things gate the commit:

1. `.vitepress/config.mts` sits inside the pending approval baseline `a8be6182` ("require_approval — pending working-tree change"), which is a **user** decision, not mine.
2. The card's own constraint: "Do not fold this into `config.mts` while that file is inside the pending approval baseline … land it after the baseline clears, or as its own commit." That constraint is respected.

⇒ **Done-ness is one commit away, and the commit is owned by `a8be6182`.** I set `wake_at = +1d` to re-verify that the commit landed; the card closes then, or moves to `user_action_needed` if the approval is still outstanding.

### Two notes for whoever commits

- The diff deliberately mixes **two** cards' nav work: this card's `channel-creator` lines and, adjacent, the `company-meetings` sidebar line (`.vitepress/config.mts:59`) plus its index row (`features/index.md:35`), which belong to `2410a44c` ("2 nav lines" in its title). Same two files, so files-scoping is clean; **ownership is not** — both cards must be cited in the commit message, or the commit split.
- Caveat on `:78-98`: the `/api/content` route table is the one claim on the page I cannot verify from this project (the router lives in `codx-api`, and I have no shell). It is an evidence gap, not a defect — recorded so the "truthful published pages" check on `68566d25` picks it up rather than rediscovering it.
